Description: Separate business from personal finances from day 1. Even if you're pre-revenue this is non-negotiable.
Do: Open on day 1 of any business activity. Route all business transactions through it.
Dont: Don't use personal account for business. Don't wait until 'the business is real'.
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ③: Takes 15 min online. No excuses.

Description: Log every business expense same day. Categorize: SaaS/Hosting/Marketing/Legal/Other.
Do: Snap receipt photos. Log in spreadsheet or Wave same day. Review weekly.
Dont: Don't save receipts for 'later'. Don't mix categories. Don't forget small purchases.
Giantiny_Note: Wave is free forever for bookkeeping. No reason not to track.

Description: Revenue - COGS = Gross Profit. Gross Profit - Expenses = Net Profit. Simple. Every month.
Do: Block 30 min on the 1st of each month. Review last month's numbers. Compare to previous month.
Dont: Don't skip months. Don't just look at revenue — profit is what matters.
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ④: Profit > Revenue. Know your margin.

Description: Match bank transactions with your records. Every transaction accounted for. Zero discrepancies.
Do: Download bank CSV. Match with your tracking. Flag any unknowns.
Dont: Don't assume everything matches. Don't ignore small discrepancies ($5 today = $500 mystery later).

Description: For B2B: send invoices promptly. For B2C: Stripe handles automatically. Track payment status.
Do: Send invoice same day as delivery. Set payment terms (Net 15 or Net 30). Follow up on day 7.
Dont: Don't be shy about collecting money. Don't accept 'check is in the mail' beyond Net 30.
Giantiny_Note: Automated Stripe billing = Giantiny ③ leverage.

Description: Move 25-30% of revenue to separate savings account for taxes. Don't touch it.
Do: On every revenue day: transfer 30% to tax savings. Treat it as untouchable.
Dont: Don't spend tax money thinking you'll earn more later. Don't forget quarterly estimates.
Giantiny_Note: Tax surprise = #1 financial killer for first-time founders.

Description: US founders: pay estimated taxes quarterly (Apr 15 Jun 15 Sep 15 Jan 15). Penalty for underpayment.
Do: Calculate quarterly: (Annual income estimate × tax rate) / 4. Pay via IRS Direct Pay.
Dont: Don't wait until April. Don't guess — use last year's income OR current projections.
Giantiny_Note: Miss this = IRS penalty. Calendar reminders non-negotiable.

Description: Cash in bank ÷ monthly burn = months of runway. Know this number at all times.
Do: Update on the 1st every month alongside P&L review. Set alerts at 6-month and 3-month thresholds.
Dont: Don't estimate — calculate exactly. Don't count expected revenue as guaranteed.
Giantiny_Note: < 6 months runway = reduce expenses. < 3 months = emergency.

Description: File annually. Schedule C for sole prop LLC. Form 1120 for C-Corp. Deadline: March 15 (corp) or April 15 (individual).
Do: Start collecting documents in January. File early to avoid rush/errors. Keep all receipts organized.
Dont: Don't file late (penalty + interest). Don't forget to deduct business expenses.
Giantiny_Note: Under $100K revenue → TurboTax DIY. Over $100K → hire CPA.

Description: Track deductible expenses: SaaS subscriptions hosting domain marketing education home office equipment.
Do: Tag every expense with category. Common deductions: software hosting marketing travel education.
Dont: Don't deduct personal expenses. Don't miss legitimate deductions (home office internet phone).
